cards.text: It's early morning, and they lead Jesus away from Caiaphas, the high priest that year (John 18:13), into the Praetorium. The Passover is coming. But the Jewish leaders stop right at the door.

cards.question: The Jewish leaders won't step inside the Praetorium. Why not?

answers.text: So they won't be defiled before the Passover
So the guards won't turn them away
So the people outside can hear the trial

cards.text: So Pilate, the governor of Judea (Luke 3:1), has to come OUT of his own building just to talk to them. He asks, "What accusation are you bringing against this man?"

cards.question: Pilate wants to hear the charge against Jesus. What do the leaders tell him?

answers.text: He wouldn't be here if He weren't a criminal
He stole money from the temple treasury
He threatened to burn down the city

cards.text: That's not a charge, friend, that's "just trust us." So Pilate tells them to take Him and judge Him by their own law.

cards.question: Pilate tells the leaders to judge Jesus by their own law, and they're happy to take Him back and do it.

cards.text: They answer that they're not permitted to execute anyone. And John says this fulfilled what Jesus had said about the kind of death He was going to die.

cards.question: Pilate goes back into the Praetorium and calls for Jesus. What's the first thing Pilate asks Him?

answers.text: Whether He is the King of the Jews
Whether He is a prophet from Galilee
Whether He has an army of followers

cards.text: Jesus answers with a question: is Pilate saying this on his own, or did others tell him? Pilate fires right back, "Am I a Jew?" That's the face I make when somebody asks if I'm the one who burned the batch.

cards.question: Pilate tells Jesus that His own people and the chief priests are the ones who handed Him over.
Pilate asks Jesus what He has done. Jesus answers that His kingdom is not of this ___. If it were, His servants would ___ to prevent His arrest.

cards.text: Pilate jumps all over that: "Then You are a king!" "You say that I am a king," Jesus answers.

cards.question: Jesus tells Pilate the reason He was born and came into the world: to testify to the ___.
Jesus came to testify to the truth. Who does He tell Pilate listens to His voice?

answers.text: Everyone who belongs to the truth
Everyone who keeps the whole law
Everyone who is a child of Abraham

cards.text: Pilate asks, "What is truth?" Then he walks right back outside, and friend, that's asking for directions and pulling away from the curb.

cards.question: Back outside, Pilate tells the leaders he finds no basis for a charge against Jesus.

cards.text: Then Pilate brings up their custom: at the Passover, he releases one prisoner to them. So he asks if they want him to release the King of the Jews.

cards.question: Pilate offers to release Jesus at the Passover. Who do they shout for instead?

cards.text: Barabbas. And John slips in one quiet little line: Barabbas was an insurrectionist.
Then Pilate takes Jesus and has Him flogged. The soldiers twist together a crown of thorns and set it on His head.

cards.question: Along with the crown of thorns, the soldiers dress Jesus in a ___ robe.

cards.text: Again and again they come up to Him saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" and slapping Him in the face.
Pilate comes out once more to let them know he finds no basis for a charge against Him. Jesus comes out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe, and Pilate says, "Here is the man!"

cards.question: Pilate brings Jesus out in the thorns and the robe. What do the chief priests and officers shout when they see Him?

cards.text: Pilate tells them to take Him and crucify Him themselves, because he finds no basis for a charge against Him. That line again, friend, for the third time. At this point it's less a ruling and more a ringtone.

cards.question: The leaders answer that they have a law, and by that law Jesus must die. What reason do they give?

answers.text: He declared Himself the Son of God
He healed people on the Sabbath

cards.text: When Pilate hears that, he's even more afraid. He goes back into the Praetorium and asks Jesus, "Where are You from?"

cards.question: When Pilate asks where He's from, Jesus gives him a full answer.

cards.text: I bet Pilate isn't used to this. The governor of Judea, left on READ, so he reminds Jesus he has authority to release Him and authority to crucify Him.

cards.question: Jesus answers that Pilate would have no authority over Him if it were not given to him from ___.
Since Pilate's authority over Jesus is given from above, who does Jesus say is guilty of greater sin?

answers.text: The one who handed Him over to Pilate

cards.text: From then on, Pilate tries to release Him. But the leaders keep shouting, and now they bring up Caesar, the emperor of Rome (Luke 3:1).

cards.question: The leaders shout that if Pilate releases Jesus, he is no friend of Caesar.

cards.text: Anyone who declares himself a king is defying Caesar, they say. When Pilate hears that, he brings Jesus out.

cards.question: Pilate brings Jesus out to a place called the Stone Pavement. What does Pilate sit on there?

cards.text: It's the day of Preparation for the Passover, about the sixth hour. And Pilate says to them, "Here is your King!"

cards.question: They shout Away with Him and Crucify Him. When Pilate asks if he should crucify their King, what do the chief priests answer?

answers.text: We have no king but Caesar
Our only King is the Lord
Let His blood be on us

cards.question: Even after all of that, Pilate sets Jesus free.

cards.text: Pilate hands Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers take Him away. We'll stop here for now, friend, but this story is far from over.

findings.problem: The joke pairs Pilate's "Am I a Jew?" with the face Papa Dorin makes when accused of burning the batch. That frames being called a Jew as being accused of something bad, which reads as a jab at a group. The comparison also misses the core action: Pilate is saying he isn't one of them, not denying blame.

rule.text: Never puts down any person or group: no jokes about age, gender, race, nationality, accents, appearance, intelligence or church denomination.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: Jesus's question, Pilate's reply and the joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus came to testify to the truth, and only the right answer repeats "truth" (Everyone who belongs to the truth). The baker can match the word instead of reasoning it out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: Pilate's reply, "That line again, friend, for the third time." and the ringtone joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Caesar" is arguable. A governor's authority over a prisoner really did come from Caesar, so a baker could argue it's right. Caesar also appears here as an answer before card 13 introduces who he is.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Caesar is called "the emperor of Rome" and cited to Luke 3:1. Luke 3:1 only names the reign of Tiberius Caesar. It doesn't say "emperor of Rome," and it doesn't say he is the Caesar in John 19:12.

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: Where the BSB says "the Jews" (John 18:28, 18:31, 19:7, 19:12), the cards say "the Jewish leaders" or "the leaders" (stop 1 cards 1, 2 and 6, stop 2 cards 7 and 13). The text names the chief priests and officers in some verses (18:35, 19:6, 19:15) but not in these. Two rules pull in opposite directions: "Call things what the text calls them" and "Leave open what the text leaves open" favor keeping "the Jews," while the hard rule against putting down any group, and the permission to fill in what the text clearly implies, favor "the leaders."
findings.question: In John's trial and crucifixion passages, should Papa Dorin keep the BSB's "the Jews" or retell it as "the Jewish leaders" or "the leaders"? Should a rule for this go into papa-dorin.md?
